newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Yizheng seen hit by low prices, high costs.
newsitem.headline: Yizheng seen hit by low prices, high costs.

text.p: Chinese polyester maker Yizheng Chemical Fibre Co Ltd's profits are likely to be hurt by lower product prices and higher material costs, analysts said on Wednesday.
Lower-than-expected results from Shanghai Petrochemical Co Ltd earlier this week also renewed gloom over the profitability of the already slack China petrochemical sector, they added.

Analysts expect Yizheng to announce on Friday the worst 1996 results among Chinese petrochemical companies with H-shares listed in Hong Kong, with net profit likely to drop 60-75 percent from 1.21 billion yuan in 1995.
The company's 1996 interim net sank 74.6 percent.
Shares in Yizheng have plunged 15 percent this week. They ended Wednesday down HK$0.05 at HK$1.34.

The fall was "on the back of the disappointing sentiment to Chinese chemical H-shares based on Shanghai (Petrochemical's) announced results, and they are pretty disappointing," said Edward Yu an analyst at Morgan Stanley Asia.
Shanghai Petrochemical said its 1996 net dropped to 1.01 billion yuan from 2.13 billion yuan in 1995.
Yu also said Yizheng recently announced its raw material prices for the second quarter were trending higher, which would affect its profitability.
The company was also facing over-supply of polyester products, which has caused a continuous fall in prices, an analyst at Vickers Ballas said.

"Their selling prices continue to drop, their raw material costs are on the rise, and the company expanded production capacity by 30 percent last year and became the largest producer in China," the Vickers analyst said.
But he added there was an indication that the company was seeing an over-supply problem. Yizheng already restricted its production growth to only five to 10 percent per year, he said.

Morgan Stanley's Yu said the average raw material cost for Yizheng actually declined last year, but the drop was not as fast as the decline in product prices so the company was seeing pressures on its profit margin.
The brokerage estimated Yizheng's polyester product prices in 1996 plunged by an average of 31 percent from a year earlier.
Yu estimated the company to face an about eight percent year-on-year fall on product prices this year while they would see a marginal easing on raw material costs.

Shanghai Petrochemcial's 161 million yuan exceptional loss from write offs of the value of some staff housing buildings following China's housing reforms also raised concerns over whether Yizheng would see similar kind of losses, brokers said.
"We saw some switching from Yizheng and Shanghai Petrochemical to Zhenhai," said Michael Ng at Sassoon Securities.
Oil refiner Zhenhai Refining & Chemical Co Ltd minimised the impact of higher material costs in 1996 and last week reported a 13.5 percent rise on its net profit for the year to 592.42 million yuan.
Jilin Chemical Industrial Co Ltd reports its 1996 results next week.
